stem: During a science class in her school in Jaipur, Meena looked at a drop of pond water under a microscope and saw tiny moving organisms. Her teacher asked the class which statement about living organisms is correct. Which one should Meena choose?

options.text: Only large plants and animals are made of cells; tiny bacteria are not cell-based organisms
All living organisms are made up of cells; some organisms have only one cell while others have many cells
Every microscopic organism consists of exactly one cell
A unicellular organism like Amoeba is not made of cells because it is too small

teacher.key_rationale: Option B states the correct rule: all living beings are made of cells, whether unicellular (one cell forming a whole organism) or multicellular (many cells building the organism). A wrongly excludes bacteria; C wrongly claims every microscopic organism is unicellular (many microbes, e.g. some algae and fungi, are multicellular); D wrongly denies that unicellular organisms are cell-based.
